extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: C-EVAL is a comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, and professional) spanning 52 diverse disciplines, ranging from humanities to science and engineering. The suite includes C-EVAL HARD, a subset of particularly challenging subjects requiring advanced reasoning abilities.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.publisher: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
extraction.citeAs: C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Exam questions were collected from mock exams, small-scale local exams, and past exam questions from top universities in China. A minor fraction of college questions were sourced from the Weipu website. Questions were primarily obtained from PDF or Microsoft Word documents on the internet, parsed, and annotated by the authors. The data collection process aimed to mitigate data contamination by avoiding official national exam questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams, small-scale local exams, past exam questions from top universities, and questions from the Weipu website. Questions were primarily sourced from PDF or Microsoft Word documents.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were parsed into structured formats, deduplicated, cleaned, and converted to LaTeX for subjects with complex mathematical notations. Questions were standardized to include exactly four choices, and incorrect choices were dropped for questions with more than four options. Explanations were generated using GPT-4 and manually revised for the development split.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations included structuring questions into a standardized format, converting LaTeX notations, and generating explanations for the development split. Explanations were first generated by GPT-4 and then manually revised by the authors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: GPT-4 for explanation generation, manual annotation by the authors for structuring and validation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Explanations were manually revised to ensure correctness and clarity. The authors cross-validated the collected data to ensure accuracy.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The authors involved in annotation and validation are affiliated with Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, and The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. Specific demographics are not provided.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/hkust-nlp/ceval. The test split labels are kept private to ensure fair use, and users submit predictions to obtain test accuracy via an online leaderboard at https://cevalbenchmark.com.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to evaluate the advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context, addressing the gap in Chinese LLM evaluation. It highlights the need for models to understand Chinese culture, history, and laws, and to improve reasoning abilities in complex scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may exhibit geographical biases towards Chinese knowledge and societal contexts. The distribution of correct answers is relatively balanced around 25%, similar to MMLU, but minor fluctuations exist.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may not fully represent the diversity of Chinese knowledge and societal contexts. It focuses on multiple-choice questions, which may not capture all aspects of advanced reasoning abilities. The test split labels are private to prevent data contamination, which may limit accessibility for some users.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-tuning for evaluating the advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. The dataset is intended to guide developers in understanding the strengths and limitations of their models.
